headline: Chips Carry the Tape at Midday as Software and Homebuilders Slip
body_html:
Semiconductors are doing the heavy lifting at midday Tuesday, with the group up 3.79% in a session whose prices are not yet final. Beyond chips the picture is more mixed. Of the 526 stocks we track, 297 are higher and 227 lower, a modest majority of gainers rather than a broad rally.

Optical and chip-equipment names are setting the pace. Fabrinet is up 16.49%, Advanced Energy 10.53% and FormFactor 9.18%. Healthcare is ahead 1.13%, industrials 1.12% and energy 0.91%, while materials add 0.33%. Revvity, up 11.72%, leads the medical names. Against that, software is off 0.57%, consumer shares are down 0.6%, and homebuilders are the weak spot at 2.61% lower.

The sharpest damage is in research and software names: Adeia is down 17.27%, Gartner 16.97% and Dynatrace 14.96%. Into the close, the question is whether chip strength holds and whether that pressure spreads through software. Traders will also watch Middle East headlines, including reports of US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, a slight uptick in oil, and talk of continuing contacts between the sides, ahead of Wednesday's session.

briefs.headline: Optical and chip gear lead the semiconductor charge
briefs.body: Semiconductors are up 3.79% at midday, the strongest group on the board. Fabrinet's 16.49% jump tops our universe, while Advanced Energy is up 10.53% and FormFactor 9.18%. Gains are concentrated in suppliers tied to chip and optical hardware. Final levels will depend on how the afternoon trades.

briefs.headline: Healthcare firms, led by life-science tools
briefs.body: Healthcare is up 1.13% so far. Revvity has gained 11.72% and Supernus Pharmaceuticals 9.66%, making them two of the day's best performers. Not everything is rising: Inspire Medical Systems is down 6.0%, a reminder that the sector's gains are driven by individual stocks rather than a uniform lift.

briefs.headline: Research and software names take a beating
briefs.body: Gartner is down 16.97% and Dynatrace 14.96%, while Adeia has lost 17.27%, the steepest drop among the stocks we track. Software as a group is off 0.57%, so the pain is concentrated in a few names. Shopify is down 7.78% and Zebra Technologies 9.44%.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders are the session's weakest corner
briefs.body: Homebuilders are down 2.61%, the worst of the eight sectors we track. Consumer shares are also lower, off 0.6%. With chips and industrials rising, the split shows investors favoring capital-spending themes over housing-linked and consumer stocks at midday.

briefs.headline: Iran headlines keep oil and the dollar in focus
briefs.body: Oil edged up after reports of a US strike on Iran's Qeshm Island, which US officials described as defensive. Iran said contacts on ending the war continue despite talks finishing without a breakthrough, and Trump voiced doubts about renewed attacks. The dollar drifted amid Mideast and midterm worries.

briefs.headline: Kimberly-Clark completes its Kenvue purchase
briefs.body: Kimberly-Clark has closed its acquisition of Kenvue, the maker of Tylenol. Attention now turns to what the combined company does next. Energy stocks are up 0.91% in our universe, while overseas, Indian shares extended gains on softer oil and strong earnings.
